los.text: Describe the main causes, presentation, investigations and principles of treatment and management of common disorders of the biliary system and pancreas
sessions: Clin 2: Biliary and pancreatic disease presentation
Clin 3: Biliary and pancreatic disease investigations
los.html:
ConditionPresentationIxManagement
Biliary colicRUQ/epigastric pain after fatty meal, <6 h, no feverUSS (stones)Analgesia (NSAIDs); elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Acute cholecystitisConstant RUQ pain >6 h, fever, Murphy's sign, ↑WCC/CRPUSS (thick wall, pericholecystic fluid)IV antibiotics, fluids, analgesia; early cholecystectomy (within 1 week); cholecystostomy if unfit
CholedocholithiasisObstructive jaundice, pale stools, dark urine, painLFTs (cholestatic: ↑ALP/GGT, ↑bilirubin), USS (dilated duct), MRCPERCP + sphincterotomy, stone extraction; then cholecystectomy
Ascending cholangitisCharcot's triad: fever/rigors + RUQ pain + jaundice (+ hypotension, confusion = Reynolds' pentad)Blood cultures, LFTs, USSSepsis 6, IV antibiotics, urgent biliary drainage (ERCP)
Acute pancreatitisSevere epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; Grey Turner's/Cullen's signs (haemorrhagic)Amylase/lipase >3× ULN; CT if diagnosis unclear or deteriorating (after 72 h)
  • Supportive: IV fluids, analgesia, nutrition (enteral), monitor
  • Treat cause (ERCP if gallstone + cholangitis; cholecystectomy same admission for mild gallstone pancreatitis).
  • Severity: Glasgow/Imrie score, APACHE II, CRP >150 at 48 h
Chronic pancreatitisChronic pain, steatorrhoea, diabetes, weight lossCT (calcification), faecal elastase (low)Alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzyme replacement (Creon), analgesia, insulin
Pancreatic cancerPainless obstructive jaundice (head), weight loss, new diabetes, back pain, Courvoisier's sign (palpable non-tender gallbladder)CT pancreas protocol, CA19-9, EUS biopsyWhipple's if resectable (~20%), chemotherapy, biliary stenting, palliative care
  • Causes of pancreatitis "I GET SMASHED": Idiopathic, Gallstones, Ethanol, Trauma, Steroids, Mumps, Autoimmune, Scorpion, Hypertriglyceridaemia/hypercalcaemia, ERCP, Drugs (azathioprine, thiazides, valproate).
    • Gallstones + alcohol = ~80%.

los.text: Describe the structure and functions (endocrine and exocrine) of the pancreas in health and disease
los.html:
Anatomy
  • Retroperitoneal (except tail)
  • Head in duodenal C-loop, neck over portal vein/SMV, body, tail to splenic hilum.
  • Main duct (Wirsung) joins CBD at ampulla of Vater (sphincter of Oddi)
  • Accessory duct (Santorini).
  • Blood: coeliac (splenic, gastroduodenal → superior pancreaticoduodenal) and SMA (inferior pancreaticoduodenal).
Exocrine (~98%)
  • Acinar cells secrete enzymes (trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase, lipase, colipase, amylase, nucleases) as inactive zymogens (+ trypsin inhibitor SPINK1) → activated in duodenum by enteropeptidase.
  • Duct cells secrete HCO₃⁻-rich fluid (CFTR; ~1.5 L/day) to neutralise acid.
  • Control: secretin (HCO₃⁻), CCK (enzymes), vagus.
Endocrine (islets of Langerhans, ~1–2%)β cells (insulin, amylin; ~70%, centre), α cells (glucagon), δ cells (somatostatin), PP cells (pancreatic polypeptide), ε cells (ghrelin).
Disease
  • Exocrine failure (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, pancreatectomy) → steatorrhoea, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, weight loss (needs >90% loss of function).
  • Autodigestion (acute pancreatitis: premature trypsin activation).
  • Endocrine failure → diabetes (T1DM: autoimmune β-cell destruction; type 3c after pancreatic disease).
  • Tumours: adenocarcinoma (ductal), neuroendocrine tumours (insulinoma: hypoglycaemia; gastrinoma: Zollinger–Ellison; glucagonoma; VIPoma), cystic neoplasms (IPMN).

los.text: Describe the metabolism of bile salts and the function of the biliary system
sessions: BMS 1: Bile acids and biliary physiology
los.html:
Bile compositionWater, bile salts, phospholipids (lecithin), cholesterol, bilirubin (conjugated), electrolytes/HCO₃⁻. ~500–1000 mL/day.
Synthesis
  • in hepatocytes from cholesterol (7α-hydroxylase, rate-limiting)
  • → primary bile acids (cholic, chenodeoxycholic)
  • → conjugated with glycine/taurine
  • → bile salts (more water-soluble, ionised, stay in lumen).
  • Colonic bacteria deconjugate and dehydroxylate → secondary bile acids (deoxycholic, lithocholic).
Function
  • Emulsify fats and form micelles (amphipathic) for fat and fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) absorption
  • Route for excreting cholesterol, bilirubin, drugs, metals (copper)
  • Bactericidal
  • HCO₃⁻ neutralises acid.
Enterohepatic circulation
  • ~95% of bile salts reabsorbed in terminal ileum (ASBT) → portal vein → liver
  • Recycled 6–10×/day.
  • Losses (~5%) replaced by synthesis.
GallbladderStores and concentrates bile (×5–10, removing water/electrolytes). CCK (fat/protein in duodenum) → gallbladder contraction + sphincter of Oddi relaxation.
Clinical
  • Ileal resection/Crohn's → bile acid diarrhoea (colestyramine) and fat malabsorption
  • Cholestasis → itch, steatorrhoea, vitamin K deficiency (↑INR)
  • Cholesterol supersaturation (↓ bile salts or ↑ cholesterol) → gallstones
  • Bile acid sequestrants lower LDL.

los.text: Describe the main causes, signs, symptoms and pathology of common disorders of the gall bladder and pancreas (pancreatitis, pancreatic cancer, gall stones)
los.html:
Gallstones (cholelithiasis)

Cholesterol stones (~80%)
  • Supersaturated bile (↑ cholesterol, ↓ bile salts/lecithin) + gallbladder hypomotility + nucleation.
  • Risk: "fat, female, fertile, forty", obesity, rapid weight loss, pregnancy, OCP, Crohn's/ileal resection, fibrates, diabetes, FHx.
Pigment stonesBlack (haemolysis: sickle cell, hereditary spherocytosis; cirrhosis) and brown (infection, in ducts).
~80% asymptomatic. Complications: biliary colic, cholecystitis, empyema, mucocele, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, pancreatitis, gallstone ileus, gallbladder cancer.
Chronic cholecystitisThickened fibrotic wall, Rokitansky–Aschoff sinuses.
Gallbladder carcinomaAdenocarcinoma; gallstones, porcelain gallbladder; poor prognosis.

Pancreatitis

Acute
  • Premature intracellular trypsin activation → autodigestion → fat necrosis (saponification with Ca²⁺ → ↓Ca²⁺, chalky deposits), haemorrhage, interstitial oedema
  • Systemic inflammation → ARDS, AKI, shock.
  • Local complications: peripancreatic fluid collections, pseudocyst (>4 weeks, no epithelial lining), necrosis (infected → abscess), splenic vein thrombosis.
Chronic
  • Repeated injury → fibrosis, loss of acini, duct dilatation with calcified protein plugs, atrophy
  • Islets relatively preserved until late.
  • Alcohol (commonest), smoking, CF, autoimmune (IgG4).

Pancreatic cancer

  • Ductal adenocarcinoma (~90%; KRAS mutation in >90%, also CDKN2A, TP53, SMAD4).
    • Precursor PanIN.
    • Risk factors: smoking, age, chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, obesity, FHx/BRCA2. ~60–70% in head → obstructive jaundice
    • body/tail present late with pain and weight loss.
    • Desmoplastic stroma, perineural invasion
    • 5-year survival <10%.
    • Trousseau's sign (migratory thrombophlebitis).
